log.msg: Two Server/ bugs found live while proving this page, neither fixed here (Server/ is out of fence tonight -- any save there restarts the live site). (1) Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js's own resolve() only strips a LEADING SLASH, unlike Tail.js's own resolve() which was fixed the same day to parse a full origin+path url -- so import.meta.resolve()'s absolute-url form (what LOG_URL/timeline.js uses for reading) silently fails every rpc:append with a flat 'append failed'. decision.about: which cards count toward the inbox's N left / the undecided queue, versus the 185 real cards on the board

options.say: a card is eligible only when it is top-level (no parent), not the owner's own card, and status === "done" -- excludes working, needs-you, and no-status cards from the count and the queue, though the rail still shows all of them
options.why: a verdict is a judgment on FINISHED work; you cannot approve the owner's own echoed sentence, an in-flight status update, or a direct yes/no operational ask (kill this session, restart the server) the same way you approve a report of something built. Measured on the real board: 185 distinct cards, 48 owner-authored, 42 with no explicit author (assistant replies), 22 working, 19 needs-you, only 50 status:done (46 once narrowed to top-level, non-owner) -- done-only is the one field that actually means "here is a finished thing to judge"

options.say: also count needs-you cards as eligible, since they are asking for the owner's attention too
options.why: would unify two kinds of owner input (judging finished work, answering an operational question) into one queue and one count, which is simpler to explain in one sentence

decision.because: a needs-you card (checked live: "Kill the stuck Fable session", "Safe to restart your server", "Your call, 2 minutes: square icon frames everywhere?") is not reporting finished work at all -- Approve/Improve has no meaning on it, and the board already has a SEPARATE mechanism for a real yes/no operational ask (say.mjs --ask, real buttons, ext/AITask's own ask/decision verbs). Folding needs-you into this queue would put Approve/Improve buttons on cards where neither button means anything, which is worse than the count being smaller. done-or-needs-you would be the better call if the owner ever says the two kinds of attention should live in one combined queue with one shared set of controls -- that is a real, larger feature (unifying verdicts and asks), not a tweak to this one's eligibility rule.
decision.rule: the owner's own words, relayed by the coordinator: "a verdict only means something on a card that reports finished work"

assign.outcome:
**The inbox now opens at 46, not 117 — and 46 is the honest number, not a target hit.** The board has 185 distinct cards; only 46 are top-level, not the owner's own words, and `status: "done"` — an actual report of finished work, the only thing Approve/Improve means anything on. Everything else (48 owner cards, 42 assistant replies with no status, 22 `working`, 19 `needs-you`) is still shown exactly as before — nothing is hidden, ineligible cards just carry no verdict controls and the count/Approve-Improve/keyboard queue skip past them, with one plain sentence on an ineligible card's own detail explaining why ("still in progress", "asking for your decision directly, not a verdict on finished work", or "no status yet"). **46 is still over the ~30 the coordinator named as roughly clearable in a sitting — said plainly, not glossed over** — because tonight is the first time any verdict has ever existed on this board: 46 finished, unjudged reports is a real backlog from before this feature shipped, not a rule tuned to hide the size of it. The decision log names the rule and the one alternative considered (folding `needs-you` in too) and why that would need a larger, separate feature (unifying verdicts with the board's own yes/no `ask` mechanism), not a tweak here.

Re-verified live end to end after the change: count reads 46 on load; an eligible `done` card ("Ready") shows real Approve/Improve, a `working` card shows "Still in progress", a `needs-you` card shows "asking for your decision directly"; pressing Approve on "Ready" dropped the count to 45 and advanced to the next ELIGIBLE undecided card, correctly skipping the working/needs-you cards in between; j/k and the arrow keys step through that same eligible queue only; Undo returned it to 46 with no residue. Every test press used `window.$VERDICT_AUTHOR` (never `owner`), and the two round-trips (approve+undo on "ready", approve+undo on "system-eval") net to zero on disk.
